Which statement is not a requirement of a pair of forces that obey Newton’s third law of motion?
A
The forces act in opposite directions.
B
The forces act on different objects.
C
The forces act on objects in contact.
D
The forces are of equal magnitude.

hints: Notice the question asks for the statement that is not required, so test each statement against the definition of a Newton third law pair.
Recall that a third law pair is same type, equal in size, opposite in direction, and acts on two different objects.
Check whether contact is needed by thinking of the Earth pulling a falling apple and the apple pulling the Earth with no contact.
walkthrough: Identify the rule: if object X exerts a force on object Y, then object Y exerts an equal and opposite force of the same type on object X.
This means the pair must have equal magnitude and opposite directions, which matches the statements about opposite directions and equal magnitude.
The pair must also involve two objects, with one force on each object, so the forces cannot both act on the same object.
Contact is not part of the rule because the law also applies to forces acting at a distance, such as gravitational attraction between Earth and Moon.
Therefore the contact statement is the one that is not required. This is option C.

A.explanation: A Newton third law pair must be opposite in direction, so this is a requirement.

B.explanation: The two forces must act on different objects, with each object exerting a force on the other.

C.explanation: Contact is not required because third law pairs also occur for non-contact forces such as gravity.

D.explanation: The two forces must be equal in magnitude at all times, so this is a requirement.
